editorial:
You are dropped into a rainy Korean province where fear spreads fast and the police are in over their heads. Three detectives chase a killer who seems always one step ahead, and their clashing styles turn every lead into a tense argument. The movie feels grounded, messy, and human, with dark humor breaking through the dread without making it feel light or easy to watch. Small-town pressure and bad evidence make every choice feel costly.

The performances are excellent, especially the way frustration and pride slowly crack each man. Pacing is steady, not flashy, and the case details keep you guessing from scene to scene. The tension comes from people, not just the crimes. It can be bleak and slow in spots, so skip it if you want nonstop action.
endingExplained: Years later, the case remains unsolved. One detective has left the force and visits the field where the first victim was found. He looks into a drainage ditch, and a young girl tells him a man was looking there recently. He stares straight into the camera, leaving you with the unsettling idea that the killer could still be nearby and the mystery is not over.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true-crime thrillers and character-driven mysteries.
